slides.title: The Conversation Happened. The CRM Needs the Right Record.
slides.subtitle: An admissions team's calling platform, read on 21 September 2026
slides.caption: When a call ends, four things have to reach the CRM: the contact's fields, a task, the call in the conversation history, and the transcript as a staff note.

slides.title: Resolve the contact first.
slides.subtitle: A phone-shaped id is searched; the first hit wins.
slides.caption: A job can be handed a phone number where a contact id should be. It searches by the number on file, and three of the four write jobs refuse to write when nothing resolves.
The operator's page for one contact, on a keyless local copy of the platform at the pinned commit with invented rows: one completed call, seven jobs, and the conversation-log write failed.

slides.title: A switch on every write. Two definitions of it.
slides.subtitle: Six sites read the dashboard flag; five read the environment.
slides.caption: On 21 September 2026 the database said live and every worker's environment said shadow, so five write paths returned a shadow response while the dashboard showed live.

The proof rows beside the jobs, on a keyless local copy of the platform at the pinned commit with invented rows: a stored id for the task and the note, none for the summary, one failed write, and the retry pointing back at it.

rows: staff-note rows carry the CRM's message id, one per call, against 1,184 completed jobs
task rows carry a task id; the row is written whether or not a task was requested
completed conversation-log jobs wrote an evidence row; the token on file sits under another location id
slides.caption: Read from the platform's own tables on 21 September 2026: one path accounted for, one with no ids, one that completed 1,099 times with nothing written. No CRM was read.

slides.title: A failed write becomes something a person can retry.
slides.subtitle: An exception with the job id; Retry Now re-enqueues it.
slides.caption: Every failure is recorded with the call, the job and the error, so the dashboard can re-enqueue the same job. Nine such rows exist, because skips and shadow responses complete cleanly.

The product's own failure record, on a keyless local copy of the platform at the pinned commit with invented rows: the error, the job id and the call id a recovery needs; the retry was made through the product's API.

slides.title: What "completed" does not prove.
slides.subtitle: A row, a switch, a token, and a CRM that was not read.
slides.caption: A completed job covers a live write, a shadow response and a clean skip alike. The record states each limit as observed, and claims nothing about the CRM's own side.
